review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: It is argued that the best students should be rewarded by their school. Many others hold a reserve opinion saying that rewarding students who show improvements is necessible. I believe that, school should reward both of these students.

Admittedly, rewarding students who have the best academic performance is undeniable. Initially, students have diligently themselves to their studies, they deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and other to study harder to win the rewards, thereby propeling towards overall academic gains. Moreover, this kind of competition can be seen in almost every aspect of life where only the best individuals are rewarded. Student are used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, leading them to achieve success in later life.

However, I strongly believe that students who show improvements should be also rewarded. Firstly, only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards. This may cause others to think that their effort is futile because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals. Therefore, students prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened that gradually lose the incentive to study. Secondly, emphasizing improvements can encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help them to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. Consequently, the constant desire to outdo themselves bring even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.

In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that rewarding students having the best academic results and students who have improvement is necessible. Therefore, it would be unfair to deny the benefits of one in favor of the other.

paragraphs: Opinions are divided over whether schools should reward students with the best academic results or whether it is more important to reward students who show progress. I believe that schools should reward both groups.

Admittedly, rewarding students with outstanding academic results is reasonable. Since students have diligently applied themselves to their studies, they deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage them and other students to study harder, thereby propelling students towards overall academic gains. Moreover, competition exists in almost every aspect of life. Students can become familiar with this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, which may prepare them for success in later life.

However, students who show progress should also be rewarded. If only a few high-achieving students receive rewards, others may think that their effort is futile because they cannot surpass those outstanding individuals. As a result, they may feel overwhelmed and disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to study. Recognizing improvement can encourage all students to work diligently and to keep improving themselves, irrespective of their current performance. The desire to outdo themselves can bring them more lasting benefits than competing against others.
In conclusion, schools should reward both students with outstanding academic results and those who make progress. It would be unfair to deny the benefits of one group in favor of the other.

task.text:
Some people think that school should reward students who show the best academic results, while others believe that it is more important to reward students who show improvements.
Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
